I will give you the basic rundown here. I won't source the stuff I'm about to share because it takes a lot of time, so take it as you will.

1) Weight is desired, not problematic.

Muscle is denser than fatty tissue. When you grow muscles you will get heavier, which is great.

2) Definition is all about bodyfat %.

You need to burn the stored fat so the muscle underneat becomes more visible.

3) Cardio does not ruin your gains.

This is a huge debate in the bodybuilding community and there is a lot of anecdotal and bogus evidence on the net. (On both sides of the discussion.) Without opening the can of worms of tossing you into it, here.

Doing proper cardio will help you get rid of some fat and help with good muscle development.

4) Getting lean is mostly diet.

Losing bodyfat is mostly about controlling your food intake. You need to work with a slight deficit and really plan your meals.

The leaner you want to get, the more effort you have to invest. Either way, I suggest using a meal planner (Like Scooby's).

Two things to consider: If you eat to lose bodyfat %, you will lose muscle mass. Which means you will plateau on your weight-volume.

If you eat to gain mass and build up strength, you will gain bodyfat %. You will advance on your weight-volume but lose some definition.

YOU CAN DO BOTH simultaneously though. But it's really fucking hard. I'm not kidding. It takes advanced meal planning and exercise/meal coordination. You will have to read up a lot if you plan on doing that. I can point to resources if so desired.

5) Forget the scale as a measurer of progress.

The weight shouldn't be your main tool to measure your progress. Aside from just checking how you look, I really recommend you get some calipers (Amazon has really great ones for 10$). They are cheap and you can get a better reading on your bodyfat%. Measure in steady intervals and see if your current plan works. You should see progress each week.

6) Be patient.

Getting rid of bodyfat% is an ardurous process, especially if you are new to the whole deal. Take it easy, don't obsess and success will follow. Keep a record of your progress, measure during the same days every week (using calipers, your bodyweight fluctuates during the day (you become lighter after hitting the bathroom for example)).

Look at the monthly trend. After some trial and error you will find out what works for your body. Then it will become really easy for you.

I hope I have not inimidated you with this. I'm here if you have any questions. I explicitely believe in your success and wish you steady progress towards your goals!
